executive_assessment.text: Half of Senegal's population and two-thirds of GDP face sea-level exposure; Dakar's population at coastal-flood risk is projected to rise 20-30% by 2050.
Summary models no-adaptation annual losses at 3-4% GDP by 2030 and 9.4% by 2050; over two million people could fall into poverty by mid-century.
Selected-sector adaptation could add about 2% GDP by 2030 and reduce climate-induced poverty by 45% versus no action.

geographic_notes.text: Senegal; Dakar: Half of Senegal's population and two-thirds of GDP face sea-level exposure; Dakar's population at coastal-flood risk is projected to rise 20-30% by 2050.

Northern Senegal; Saint-Louis: The diagnostic says northern Senegal is projected to experience more frequent extreme droughts, particularly in Saint-Louis; its cited CCDR scenarios estimate annual GDP losses of 3.6–4% by 2030 and 7–9.4% by 2050 without adaptation.

Senegal; Saint-Louis; Matam; Tambacounda; Louga: Senegal’s NDC reports declining rainfall, rising mean temperature, sea-level rise, and disruptions to cultivable land, water, and fisheries; it identifies northern regions, especially Saint-Louis, as facing a 20–30% increase in extreme-drought frequency, and identifies more wet extremes in Matam, Tambacounda, and Louga under its low-warming scenario.

known_gaps.text: The full Senegal CCDR main report exceeded the available reader’s content limit; claims from that product are limited to its opened executive summary and separately opened World Bank diagnostic.
The reviewed Senegal sources do not establish a country-specific climate-conflict pathway; none is asserted here.
